paper_title: Can We Edit LLMs for Long-Tail Biomedical Knowledge

model_annotation: This line plot illustrates the accuracy (ACC %) of five different methods—Base, MEND, FT, MEMIT, IKE, and ROME—as a function of the co-occurrence number, which is plotted on the x-axis using a logarithmic scale ranging from 10⁰ (1) to 10³ (1000). The y-axis represents accuracy in percentage, ranging from 60% to 80%, with tick marks at regular intervals of 5%. The Base method (black line with circle markers) starts at approximately 64% accuracy and increases steadily to about 71%. The MEND method (brown line with diamond markers) begins at around 70% and rises to approximately 80%. The FT method (blue line with triangle markers) starts at about 65% and increases to roughly 73%. The MEMIT method (purple line with star markers) begins at approximately 70% and trends upward to about 77%. The ROME method (green line with square markers) starts at around 75% and shows the highest performance, increasing to approximately 83%. All lines exhibit a generally increasing trend as the co-occurrence number increases, with ROME consistently outperforming the others across the entire range.
